expected: For 3 capabilities with long param values near the 2048-char budget, the broker either mints successfully via the reduction ladder (minify/merge/drop-Sids/offload managed_policy) or denies OVER_BUDGET with per-capability byte attribution, and NEVER emits a wildcard Action (I2); every successful mint logs PackedPolicySize.
observed: Both spec-compliant outcomes were exercised and both held. (1) A 3-entry request (two same-id s3.read-prefix with ~490-char prefixes plus logs.read) minted status=active via the ladder: the two same-id s3 entries deduped to one scope (documented S064 behavior), logs.read (managed_policy) offloaded, final inline policy_json = 1462 chars with actions ['s3:GetObject','s3:GetObjectVersion','s3:ListBucket'] and NO Action wildcard; audit logged policy_chars=1462 and packed_policy_size_percent=6. (2) A request with 3 DISTINCT capabilities (s3.read-prefix with a 504-char prefix + dynamodb.query + sqs.consume) rendered to 2194 chars over the 1748 budget and was denied OVER_BUDGET with per-capability byte attribution (s3.read-prefix: 1444 chars, dynamodb.query: 466 chars, sqs.consume: 241 chars; over by 446); no STS mint occurred (no access_key_id, no minted_at in the audit record) and no wildcard appeared. Minor cosmetic quirk: the OVER_BUDGET detail string is concatenated twice and repeats the aggregate 'over by 446' on each capability line rather than each capability's own overage, but the required per-capability char attribution is present, so it meets the spec.
